proposals.title: Douglas W. Diamond — Financial Intermediation as Delegated Monitoring: A Simple Example, Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond Economic Quarterly 82(3), 51–66 (Summer 1996)
proposals.use: Primary conceptual route for avoiding duplicated monitoring and accounting for the cost of delegated incentives. The chapter proves its own finite enforcement/public-benefit game and financing comparison; it does not assume Diamond's optimal-debt or diversification results.
proposals.verification: Actual 16-page official PDF retrieved, not just a search result. Inspected opening/service discussion and Section 1 monitoring/delegation-cost discussion on printed pages 51–54, and the opening monitoring-the-monitor discussion on printed page 59. Root preparation had already inspected the opening four PDF pages; author reopened the actual body and read the stated additional scope. Historical statistics and reserve statements are excluded. The toy enforcement removes a private diversion payoff under explicitly assumed verifiable completion; it is not presented as a reproduction of the paper's contract or a general delegated-monitoring theorem.

proposals.title: Douglas W. Diamond and Philip H. Dybvig — Bank Runs, Deposit Insurance, and Liquidity, Journal of Political Economy 91(3), 401–419 (June 1983)
proposals.use: Primary source for private liquidity needs, sequential random service, mutual residual claims and post-deposit run best replies. Original utility, calibration and proof in the chapter establish only the stated feasible insurance comparison and two post-deposit equilibria; no optimal-insurance or policy theorem is imported.
proposals.verification: UChicago institutional repository landing page actually read, identifying authors, June 1983 publication, DOI 10.1086/261155 and copyright-holder permission for repository availability. Actual 332510-byte, 19-page PDF retrieved from https://knowledge.uchicago.edu/records/3sa4m-hvw53/files/Bank-Runs-Deposit-Insurance-and-Liquidity.pdf?download=1 through the standard-library HTTP reader and pdftotext in memory. Read printed pages 404–410, especially Section II on technology, private types and storage (405–406), consumption allocation (407), random sequential service and mutual sharing (408), and equilibrium/participation qualifications (409–410). The web parser rejected this download's application/octet-stream MIME type; the earlier Minneapolis PDF route returned an error. Those failed requests were not counted as body verification. Later optimal suspension, random aggregate demand and government-insurance proofs were not audited and are not assumed.

reused_sources.additional_author_inspection: On 9 October 2026 reopened the actual 14-page official primary PDF. Read printed pages 14–19 / PDF pages 1–6 for the reserve/deposit distinction, origination, repayment, external payment settlement, funding and risk limits. Reuses the accepted source metadata rather than proposing a duplicate record. The present chapter uses its own two-bank numbers and later income timing. No historical UK aggregate percentage, reserve requirement or central-bank accommodation statement is presented as current or universal.

scope_limit: Sources support only the identified concepts and body passages. Screening Bayes calculations, all finite game and ledger cases, the shifted reciprocal utility comparison, proofs, exercises and code are original. Source retrieval and author review are not external academic certification. No current legal or regulatory definition is needed or asserted. Adjacent accounting and later liquidity/regulation chapters supply their own source scopes.
